memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now Laban had two daughters; the name of the older was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel. Leah had weak eyes, but Rachel had a lovely figure and was beautiful. Jacob was in love with Rachel and said, 'I'll work for you seven years in return for your younger daughter Rachel.'" - Gen 29:16-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Laban has two daughters — Leah, the older, and Rachel, the younger and strikingly beautiful. Jacob falls deeply in love with Rachel and makes a bold offer: he will work seven years to marry her. In that culture a groom often gave a gift or payment to the bride's family, but seven years of labour was a remarkable price. Jacob considered Rachel worth every day of it.

There is something admirable in a love willing to commit and to pay a real cost. Jacob did not want Rachel cheaply or casually; he was ready to invest years of his life for her. In a world that often wants love without commitment or sacrifice, Jacob's willingness to work long and hard for the one he loved stands out.

Yet we should also notice the shadow already forming. The text quietly contrasts the two sisters — Rachel is praised for her beauty, while Leah is passed over. Human love so often runs after outward attractiveness while overlooking others. We will see the heartache this causes as the story unfolds.

Real love is willing to commit and to give. But the deepest love looks past mere appearance to the heart. Let us learn to value people as God does — not by outward beauty, but by who they truly are (1 Pet 3:3-4).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is my love willing to commit and to pay a real cost?
2. Do I value people by outward appearance or by the heart?
3. Who around me is being overlooked, as Leah was?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, teach me a love that commits and gives, and help me to see people as You do — not by their appearance, but by their heart. Amen.
